report.source_text: The targeted RNA sequencing by Archer FusionPlex identified an NTRK2 rearrangement joined with the novel 5' fusion partner ATG16L1. The genomic breakpoints were located in introns of the two genes, resulting in an ATG16L1 (exon 9)::NTRK2 (exon 16) in-frame fusion transcript (Figure 2A). Reinspection of the copy number alteration (CNA) plot inferred from the methylation data showed an evident loss in chromosome band 2q37.1 with a breakpoint within the ATG16L1 gene, resulting in the loss of the 3ʹ end. No apparent CNA could be seen in chromosome band 9q21.33 (NTRK2). However, zooming in on the gene level of NTRK2 hints at an copy number imbalance between the 5ʹ and 3ʹ ends, with lower levels of the 5ʹ end of NTRK2 (Figure 2B). To confirm the results, interphase fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) analysis with an NTRK2 break-apart probe was performed, verifying a DNA rearrangement of NTRK2 (Figure 2C).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old boy presented with personality change, visual disturbance, and vomiting. Initial MRI in September 2019 revealed a 5x5x7 cm intraventricular tumor with growth into the temporal lobe, hypothalamus, and basal ganglia. Resected tissue pathology showed features suggesting a low-grade glioma (LGG), including relatively small cell nuclei, few Rosenthal fibers, occasional mitosis, GFAP and synaptophysin positivity, and a low Ki-67 proliferation rate. Immunohistochemistry ruled out other common brain tumor entities (normal TP53, preserved ATRX, negative H3K27 mutation). Molecular Neuropathology Brain classifier confirmed the diagnosis as BRAF-wildtype Pilocytic Astrocytoma (PA), WHO grade 1. Further molecular testing identified an ATG16L1::NTRK2 fusion transcript and NTRK2 rearrangement, leading to referral for the SCOUT clinical trial. Oral treatment with larotrectenib was initiated in June 2022. After 8 months of treatment (February 2023), the patient achieved a complete response, with all measurable and non-measurable lesions no longer detectable. This complete response was sustained at the last follow-up in April 2024, after one year and 10 months of treatment.
